findings.body: Any authenticated caller can set `body.accountId` and load a different account. The handler takes that value whenever it is present and queries `db.accounts.findUnique` with it, so `{"accountId": "<victim>"}` returns that account's record. Restrict the override to a verified staff role on `caller` (and keep `caller.accountId` for everyone else), or move staff lookup to a separate staff-only route.

summary:
Any authenticated caller can look up another account by sending `accountId` in the JSON body. `getAccount` previously scoped the query to `caller.accountId` from `auth(req)`; this change substitutes a client-supplied id with no staff-role (or other authorization) check before `findUnique`.

That is an IDOR on a staff-tool path that still sits on the same handler regular users hit. Gate the override on a verified staff role, or put staff lookup on a separate, staff-only route that rejects mismatched ids for everyone else.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head handler sets `id` from `body.accountId ?? caller.accountId` with no staff/role check, so any authenticated caller can load another account. The base version only used `caller.accountId`, confirming this is a real IDOR regression.
